quest.title: Ever Beneath the Waves
quest.description: A strange block of ice floats upon the water. A mysterious voice comes to you over a pipe system, claiming that there is a wooden cabin hanging upside down beneath the ice. Clear the brash ice nearby, and you might cause the cabin to show its true form...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x250, Primogem x30, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x3

talks.objective: Find the source of the voice

dialogues.speaker: Voice Beneath the Ice
dialogues.text: I hear footsteps, traveler by the shore. Please, if you would, halt a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, there it is again, the voice from beneath the water! Uh-oh, it isn't coming from some sorta ghost, is it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Voice Beneath the Ice
dialogues.text: Be not afraid, traveler. You speak of ghosts, and indeed, I might be considered a ghost of history. Yet I assure you, I mean no ill.

dialogues.speaker: Voice Beneath the Ice
dialogues.text: The huge floe you see before you is the foundation of my habitation. At the moment, my dwelling has been trapped in brash ice and now hangs upside down on the surface of this lake.

dialogues.speaker: Voice Beneath the Ice
dialogues.text: If you could lend me a hand <color=cyan>and rid the lake of all this brash ice</color>, you would have my utmost gratitude.

talks.objective: Clear the brash ice in the area

dialogues.speaker: Cryo Cabin
dialogues.text: I cannot thank you enough, travelers by the shore. Your help has brought me relief from my troubles.

dialogues.speaker: Cryo Cabin
dialogues.text: If you'd be so kind, could you <color=cyan>draw this cabin to the shore</color>, that it shall not have to remain ever stagnant upon the water's surface?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Y'know, Paimon's getting kinda curious about this guy! If we drag his house ashore, d'you think we could get a good look at him?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And how will we do this?

dialogues.speaker: Cryo Cabin
dialogues.text: Please look for Prime Ice devices around you and place them in suitable spots. They will then pull the cabin in.

talks.objective: Talk to the person in the cabin
Bring the wooden cabin to shore

dialogues.speaker: Cryo Cabin
dialogues.text: My thanks, travelers by the shore. I will remember this worthy deed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey now, shouldn't you thank people in person?

dialogues.speaker: Cryo Cabin
dialogues.text: I apologize and beg pardon for my disrespect. I am not unaware of worldly etiquette, but my face has not seen the sun for many years, and I fear its sight shall offend you.

dialogues.speaker: Cryo Cabin
dialogues.text: Please forgive this excess personage, please absolve this last scion of old snowfield-dwelling nobility, doomed to be forgotten by time, whose name is Chulkaturin.

dialogues.speaker: Churkaturin
dialogues.text: Please forgive him his choice, for he has long ensconced himself in this cabin on the ice, never to set foot on Snezhnayan land, and thus has he lived for three hundred and twenty-one years.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait. Are you serious... Have you not left this wooden house for three hundred-plus years!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're not human, then.

dialogues.speaker: Churkaturin
dialogues.text: That is so, travelers by the shore. I am a ghost of the past, long-forgotten, a relic of an era that still belonged to the fae.

dialogues.speaker: Churkaturin
dialogues.text: More than three hundred years ago, we were utterly uprooted from this land. The curtain fell on the old era, and there is no longer any place for us here.

dialogues.speaker: Churkaturin
dialogues.text: Our glory has been reduced to dust. Our homeland... The snow poplars... They lie in the snow, cut down to the last.

dialogues.speaker: Churkaturin
dialogues.text: Some who share my memories of those times have disappeared, and others have broken with their pasts. At the end, at the last, only I am left.

dialogues.speaker: Churkaturin
dialogues.text: I could not choose between those two roads, and so I entrusted my fate to this home on ice...

dialogues.speaker: Churkaturin
dialogues.text: I used felled snow poplars to construct it, and have since allowed it to carry me along, across lakes and rivers alike.

dialogues.speaker: Churkaturin
dialogues.text: The wind shall rise shortly, and the flowing waters will carry my destiny off.

dialogues.speaker: Churkaturin
dialogues.text: Perhaps we shall meet again, shorebound travelers. Should that time come, and you remain interested in my tales, I shall again speak of them to you.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The wooden cabin on the ice slowly drifts along with the current until it disappears from sight.

talks.objective: Talk to the person in the cabin
